thread.title: Southwest Airlines putting new music service on 690 aircraft

author: Lewis Lazare
title: Southwest Airlines putting new music service on 690 aircraft
text: – Reporter, Chicago Business Journal May 24, 2018, 7:40am EDT Southwest Airlines just introduced a new music offering that will be available on 690 Wi-Fi-equipped planes in the low-fare carrier’s fleet. Southwest is partnering with iHeartMedia, a giant in the radio industry, and its iHeartRadio unit to roll out an all-in-one digital music and livestreaming radio service for passengers on Southwest flights. Southwest is the dominant carrier out of Raleigh Durham International , a popular airport for Triad travelers. The music offering will be accessible through Southwest’s onboard entertainment portal. The available iHeartRadio music will include a variety of musical genres, including alternative rock, country, hip hop, R&B, Top 40 and more. Passengers will have the option of choosing a favorite radio station or selecting from hundreds of artists to create their customized artist radio station featuring music from that artist and those with similar music styles. Southwest’s new collaboration with iHeartRadio also will give passengers access to curated station themes such as “Pass the Time” and “Kids Zone” to listen to inflight. The iHeartRadio product will be free of charge to Southwest passengers, who can access it via their personal devices. Once activated, the music will continue to play as long as the Southwest entertainment portal is open in a tab. Customers also will be able to access the iHeartRadio offering on Southwest flights via the iHeartRadio app. Southwest (NYSE: LUV) cautioned, however, that because of licensing restrictions, the new music service might not be available on international flights. The partnership with iHeartMedia comes after Southwest had a short-lived relationship with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) and its Beats Music unit, which also provided a menu of music for listening on flights. But that relationship, which began in late 2014, quietly ended a while ago without any explanation from Southwest or Apple. iHeartMedia (OTC: IHRTQ) operates 849 radio stations nationwide, making it one of the last media companies in the U.S., but a company that is also financially-challenged. iHeartMedia filed for bankruptcy protection last March.
